idiom_name: _Generic selection over the type of the controlling expression (C11; the <tgmath.h> technique)
implementation_notes: C has no overloading, so the ladder collapses into one compile-time selection: _Generic matches the type of its controlling expression against a list of type names and yields the expression of the matching association, without evaluating the others - the tag is the static type itself, and the association list plays the role of the overload set. What replaces the classic structure: _Generic picks a function designator (as <tgmath.h> does for cbrt/cos), and calling through the selected pointer is the implementation ladder. The classic form is still justified with hand-written tag structs plus a function-pointer table when the discriminating tag is only known at run time, or when the project is stuck below C11; there is no fallback ranking, so each selection is a single level with an optional default.
pitfalls: The controlling expression undergoes lvalue conversion, which strips qualifiers and decays arrays, so char const and char match the same association and "abc" matches char* - a defect that had to be fixed by DR 481; write +X or &X to control which type is matched.

Associations select expressions, not statements, and every association must still be a valid expression for the compiler: put each implementation in a function and let _Generic choose the function designator, as <tgmath.h> does, instead of trying to inline statement blocks.

There is no ranking or fallback between associations: a missing case is either a hard compile error or lands on default:, so the 'specificity ladder' of the C++ form has to be rebuilt by hand (or given up).
sources: Microsoft Learn, Generic selection (C11, with the <tgmath.h> type-dependent macro example), https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/c-language/generic-selection
C DR 481: Controlling expression of _Generic primary expression (lvalue conversion, qualifiers, arrays), https://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg14/issues/c11c17/issue0481.html
